1. Core Clinical Tension: A 57-year-old rural resident presents with a massive 27-cm fluid-filled abdominal mass causing gross abdominal distension and dullness without systemic constitutional decline, closely mimicking a giant mesenteric cyst, mucinous peritoneal carcinomatosis, or ovarian/retroperitoneal cystadenocarcinoma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint is positioned after abdominal physical examination, unremarkable routine biochemical labs, ultrasound, and cross-sectional CT scanning revealing the massive calcified fluid collection with undulating membranes and hepatic cysts, strictly before specific send-out serology results and exploratory laparotomy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Cystic abdominal neoplasia (e.g., pseudomyxoma peritonei or cystadenoma) lacks characteristic thick curvilinear parietal wall calcifications and concurrent multivesicular hepatic cystic lesions. Benign mesenteric cysts lack internal germinal membranes and multilocular intrahepatic daughter cysts.
case_prompt:
A 57-year-old male originally from a rural area presented with a 12-month history of mild, intermittent abdominal pain accompanied by progressive abdominal distension and a sensation of generalized abdominal heaviness. He noted no fevers, night sweats, anorexia, jaundice, vomiting, or deterioration of his general health. He had no prior chronic medical history or previous surgical procedures.

On physical examination, the abdomen was markedly distended with diffuse dullness to percussion. There was no localized tenderness, guarding, or rigidity. Vital signs were normal, and sclerae were anicteric.

Routine admission laboratory tests, including complete blood count, renal function, and liver chemistries, were within normal reference ranges. Bedside abdominal ultrasonography revealed a large, heterogeneous intra-abdominal mass of indeterminate origin. Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a massive, well-defined fluid-density formation measuring 27 cm x 26 cm x 16 cm displaying distinct parietal calcifications and internal membranes, causing extensive displacement of bowel loops. This prominent collection was accompanied by multiple intrahepatic cystic lesions of varying sizes and stages distributed across both the right and left lobes of the liver.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Mesenteric Cyst or Retroperitoneal Cystadenoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A massive 27-cm intra-abdominal cystic mass in an adult can mimic a mesenteric or retroperitoneal cystic neoplasm. However, simple or neoplastic mesenteric cysts lack internal undulating membranes and thick peripheral calcifications, and do not account for multifocal companion hepatic cysts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The ultrasound shows a large heterogeneous abdominal mass whose origin is difficult to determine. A requested abdominal CT scan finds: bulging abdominal fluid formation not elevated measuring 27cm/26cm/16cm seat of parietal calcification and membranes displacing the digestive structures

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Abdominal distension with diffuse dullness on percussion and massive fluid accumulation can indicate mucinous peritoneal carcinomatosis; however, the well-circumscribed cystic capsule, internal membranes, parietal calcification, and absence of constitutional cachexia favor a chronic parasitic etiology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He presented for 12 months of mild abdominal pain and intermittent aggravated by abdominal distention and feeling of heaviness without other associated signs or deterioration of the general condition. Clinically there is abdominal distension with generalized dullness.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: CT characteristics showing an exophytic multi-stage calcified cyst with internal membranes combined with multiple hepatic cysts, positive parasitic serology, and surgical resection confirming an exophytic liver hydatid cyst extending into the inframesocolic compartment established the diagnosis of Echinococcosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Apart from a positive serology, the remainder of the biological examination was unremarkable... A requested abdominal CT scan finds: bulging abdominal fluid formation not elevated measuring 27cm/26cm/16cm seat of parietal calcification and membranes displacing the digestive structures... this formation is associated with multiple hepatic hydatid cysts... The patient was operated and the exploration found a hydatid cyst of segment III adhered to the gall bladder and extending through a narrow path at the level of the mesocolic stage where it develops to create a huge cystic mass of 30cm long axis

editor_comments: Standardized admission diagnostic case for echinococcosis (exophytic hepatic and peritoneal hydatid cyst). Breakpoint cleanly set after CT scan imaging prior to serology return and surgical pericystectomy.
